artifacts.summary: Research report: hook/test naming and registration surface confirmation, claude-refresh.sh Family B pgrep-f gap finding, shared-library rejection rationale, Rule 4 lifecycle ruling, structural precedent comparison (guard-destructive-git.sh vs validate-no-task-references.sh), and implementation recommendations.

memory_candidates.content: claude-refresh.sh's Family B waiter classifier (build_waiter_family(), scripts/claude-refresh.sh) matches only the literal substring 'grep -q' combined with until/while + sleep. It does NOT match 'pgrep -f' at all (pgrep -f is not a substring of 'grep -q'), despite its own header comment implying broader coverage. Any future consumer wanting to reuse this inventory as a drop-in regex set must verify coverage against the actual code, not the header prose.

For a new single-hazard-class blocking PreToolUse Bash hook in this repo, validate-no-task-references.sh is a better structural template than guard-destructive-git.sh: single parse-once stdin read, one conjunction/match test, one exit-2+stderr block, fail-open on every parse/dependency failure. guard-destructive-git.sh's multi-branch REASON/OVERSTAGE_REASON structure exists specifically because it guards several independent hazard classes in one file, which a single-shape hook does not need.

root-files/settings.json in this agent-system is a first-install-only template (per loader.lua's INSTALL_ONCE_ROOT_FILES): it is copied only when no project .claude/settings.json exists yet and is never overwritten on subsequent deploy/reload. A hook registration added there cannot reach an already-deployed consumer repo. The live update path for settings.json hook registrations is merge-sources/settings-hooks.json, confirmed independently by scripts/verify-deploy.sh's own remediation string.
